editorial:
Imagine walking into a room to interview a criminal, only to find out that the victims actually like him. That is exactly where you start with this story. You follow Musa, a law student who thinks he has the world figured out. He goes to visit Davud, a man locked up for kidnapping four women. But instead of finding scared victims, Musa finds women who feel like they found a deeper truth because of Davud. It feels like a deep conversation between two people where the lines between right and wrong start to blur. You will find yourself questioning if the law actually brings justice or if it just follows a set of boring rules.

What really works here is how the movie makes you think without being too heavy. The acting is solid, and the slow build-up keeps you guessing about whether Davud is a genius or just a clever liar. Some might find the pace a bit slow, but if you like movies that challenge your brain, you will love it.
endingExplained: As the movie wraps up, you realize that Davud was not just kidnapping people, but leading them into a strange spiritual trap. Musa becomes so obsessed with Davud's ideas that he starts to lose his own sense of reality. The ending shows that the law cannot fix everything, but it also warns you that following a charismatic leader can be dangerous. Musa ends up changed, leaving you to wonder if he was enlightened or just fooled.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological dramas and stories about morality.
